subject: MAP weekly: performance yardstick review and tuning priorities
messages:
From: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@heliostx.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint focus — perf data and meeting slot?

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the run-through last week. As we move deeper into the MAP I want to make sure this week's checkpoint is focused on concrete performance measurements (latency/throughput) and the practical tuning path for our P1 inference flow. Specifically:

- Can Redwood share the latest end-to-end benchmark artifacts (99th / p95 / median) for our config?
- Do you have a short runbook for the tuning knobs we discussed (batching, quantization, KV cache)?
- Can we lock a 30-min slot this Thursday to review results and agree on owners for the next sprint?

Attaching our internal SLA draft so you can see the target ranges we care about. Ideally we want to validate whether the 99th percentile for the P1 prompt is under ~300ms at expected QPS.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Chang
Head of Production Engineering
Helios Therapeutics

Attachment: helios-sla-draft-20280706.pdf (pdf)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@heliostx.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint focus — perf data and meeting slot?

Lydia — thanks, this is exactly the right framing.

Quick summary and what I attached:
- redwood-map-benchmark-summary-20280704.pdf: consolidated run of your P1 prompts at the committed config (batching=dynamic, quant=bf16→int8 candidate). Includes median/p95/p99 by endpoint and by prompt length.
- latency-results-20280704.csv: raw per-request latencies with request payload hashes and sequence lengths.

Proposed 30-min review: Thu Jul 7, 2028 at 11:00am PT. If that doesn't work, I can do Thu 2:00pm PT as backup.

Initial notes from the run:
- Median well under 100ms for short prompts; 99th for long P1 prompts is ~420ms on current config (we saw a tail in the 1–1.5s range under bursty load).
- Primary suspects: prompt-length variance + occasional KV-cache cold starts during simultaneous canary traffic.

Suggested tactical next steps (owners):
1) Run a targeted quantization A/B with your P1 prompt set (canary config): Owner: Rafael — validate accuracy delta and p99 impact. ETA: Jul 11.
2) KV-cache warmup policy + gating on first-token cold start — small runtime change we can test in dedicated pool: Owner: Neha — propose gating thresholds and test harness. ETA: Jul 14.
3) Adjust continuous batching thresholds for the P1 endpoint to favor latency over throughput during ramp windows: Owner: Marcus — provide batching schedule and simulated QPS tests. ETA: Jul 10.
4) Create a small playback set for regression alerts tied to these MAP prompts: Owner: Monica — add to Optimize and hook alerts. ETA: Jul 12.

If we agree I will share a condensed deck before Thu's sync with p95/p99 highlights and a short list of risk mitigations.

Rafael
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-map-benchmark-summary-20280704.pdf (pdf), latency-results-20280704.csv (csv)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: note on prompt length distribution / p99 spike

Team — quick internal context ahead of the Helios sync: I dug into latency-results-20280704.csv and attached a short distribution.

Findings: the top 3% of requests (by seq length) are responsible for ~65% of the p99 mass. A couple of these are >1.2k tokens which triggers different attention-kernel paths and increased kernel swap overhead.

Proposal: add a gating rule for P1 that sends >800-token requests to a separate background pool (lower parallelism, higher memory), and short-circuit KV-cache warmup for repeated session IDs. I can draft the gating thresholds and a small simulation by Mon Jul 10.

Attachment: prompt-length-distribution.csv (csv)

Neha
From: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@heliostx.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint focus — perf data and meeting slot?

Thanks Rafael — I reviewed the summary. A few clarifying asks before Thu: 

1) Our SLA ask: can Redwood commit (for production Dedicated) to a 99th percentile <300ms for P1 at 40 QPS sustained? If not commit, can you provide a realistic range and the main levers we'd use to get there?
2) For canary rollout, what is the safe traffic ramp plan you recommend (percent steps + monitoring gates)? We need specifics so we can map to our change control.

Attaching our SLA doc as context (same file as before). Also, please flag any tests we should run on our side before your canary so we avoid false positives in post-deploy alerts.

Lydia

Attachment: helios-sla-draft-20280706.pdf (pdf)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chang <lydia.chang@heliostx.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Helios Procurement <procurement@heliostx.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP checkpoint notes (11 Jul) — decisions, owners, next steps

Team / Lydia — summary from our checkpoint this morning and explicit action log. Thanks for the focused discussion.

Meeting notes (condensed):
- Reviewed redwood-map-benchmark-summary-20280704.pdf and latency CSV; confirmed p99 tail driven by long prompt variance and cache cold starts.
- Agreed we will not immediately rewrite SLA language; instead we will provide a validated target range for Dedicated on Jul 18 once quant A/B and KV gating tests finish.
- Canary rollout plan agreed (high-level): 5% → 20% → 50% → 100% with 30-min steady-state gates and p99/p95 guardrails; automatic rollback on error-rate or p99 increase >30%. Marcus to formalize the gate criteria.

Action items (owner - due):
- Rafael: Run quantization A/B on P1 prompt set, capture accuracy delta and p99 impact; publish test report. Due: 2028-07-11 (end of day).
- Marcus: Draft canary ramp steps, monitoring gates, and a smoke-playbook (Jira MAP-1122). Due: 2028-07-12.
- Neha: Prototype KV-cache gating and simulated warmup; provide microbench harness and thresholds. Due: 2028-07-14.
- Monica: Create playback set and hook alerts in Optimize; add map testcases to our alerting runbook. Due: 2028-07-12.
- Helios (Lydia / Engineering): Run a short local playback (10k samples) the day before canary to verify signal fidelity. Suggested window: Jul 17.

Files shared: redwood-map-benchmark-summary-20280704.pdf, latency-results-20280704.csv, prompt-length-distribution.csv, helios-sla-draft-20280706.pdf

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HL-2028-058), MAP ticket (https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/MAP-1122), shared drive folder with artifacts (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-map-benchmarks).

If there are no objections I'll mark the actions in the MAP and send calendar invites for the follow-ups (quant A/B review + canary prep).

Rafael
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
